t: For expenses necessary to cany out the provisions of the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 (15 U.S.C. 205), $2,474,000.

fable.w: This section only appropriates money to carry out the Metric Conversion Act of 1975. The tempting reading is that the referenced Act created a Metric Board with non-federal members, but this section itself sets up no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. A funding provision that merely cites another statute does not bring any outside party into a federal decision.
fable.s: For expenses necessary to cany out the provisions of the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 (15 U.S.C. 205), $2,474,000.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation of funds for the execution of a specific act. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) before a decision is made. It merely allocates money.
qwen_block.s: For expenses necessary to cany out the provisions of the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 (15 U.S.C. 205), $2,474,000.

opus.w: This section only appropriates funds to carry out an existing Act. It does not require or allow outside parties to take part in any federal decision. The underlying Act may set up a board with outside members, but a bare reference to that Act is not participation, just as the funding provision in Example 1 was not.
opus.s: For expenses necessary to cany out the provisions of the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 (15 U.S.C. 205), $2,474,000.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing funds for expenses related to the Metric Conversion Act. It does not explicitly require or recommend any specific participatory process such as public hearings, comment periods, or advisory committees involving outside parties. The mere authorization of funds does not constitute a requirement for participation under the provided definition.
qwen_chat.s: For expenses necessary to cany out the provisions of the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 (15 U.S.C. 205), $2,474,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that carrying out the Metric Conversion Act inherently involves public participation (e.g., public education, industry consultation). However, the text provided is merely an appropriation clause authorizing funds. It does not explicitly mandate any specific participatory process (like hearings, comments, or advisory boards) within this section itself. The definition requires the section to *recommend or require* participation. An appropriation for general expenses does not explicitly require a participatory mechanism.
